text:
If I love the beauty and serve her, does that alarm you? Do you deem me vile, foolish, witless? She has goods for every taste. For love of her I wear dagger and shield and kill. When someone comes I seize a jug and slip quietly from the room. Then I bring him cheese and bread, embrace him, and if he pays well say, “When will you return? When she is in heat, friend, we await you in the brothel where we earn our bread.”

But if dawn comes and he brought no money, woe to Margot! I rage, cannot look at her, want to cut her throat. I take her clothes outside and threaten to sell them. She stands like Antichrist, and I might kill her there, but by Christ's death she swears I will not. Thus we fight in the brothel where we earn our bread.

Then peace returns; she farts more criminally than a cannon shot, laughs and strikes me, then says, “Climb on!” as she settles. We sleep like clogs, both drunk. If she wakes and her belly still demands, she rises and mounts me. “She crushes us!” the bed and I groan, “Your lust breaks us apart!” in the brothel where we earn our bread.

Rain or thunder, my bread is secure. I am vicious and found a vicious woman. I swear I know not which is worse. Filth seems beautiful, honor disgusts us and we drive it away in the brothel where we earn our bread.

translation.title: Ballad of Fat Margot
